tldr: In physics-based humanoid character control, HetSkills proposes a control framework that progressively and seamlessly integrates and reuses heterogeneous skills—motion tracking, text-to-motion generation, motion completion from partial observations, and downstream task adaptation—through a shared latent space and a frozen decoder.
hero_caption: Overall view of HetSkills. From left to right, it illustrates motion tracking, text-to-motion generation, motion completion, and downstream task adaptation. Skills with completely different training data and task objectives comfortably coexist on a single physics decoder and a unified latent space.
overview:
In physics-based humanoid character control, acquiring natural and diverse skills has long been a dream. However, prior approaches typically trained separate controllers from scratch for each distinct purpose—such as tracking, text instructions, or specific tasks—or only used pre-trained models as external regularizers. As a result, it has been extremely difficult to progressively accumulate skills acquired from different data sources and training stages into a single body and combine them at will.

To address this, the authors came up with a new framework called "HetSkills." The core idea is to decompose the body into arms and body trunk, construct a deterministic "unified latent space," and completely freeze the decoder that computes joint torques from it once trained. It first learns a robust motion tracking skill to establish a solid control foundation. Then, on top of this frozen decoder, modules for text-to-motion generation, motion completion from sparse observations (like VR or keyframes), and downstream task adaptation via language instructions are progressively added onto the very same latent space.

Large-scale experiments in a physics simulator (Isaac Lab) validated the effectiveness of this framework. In text-to-motion generation, it achieved a high success rate of 81.7% even under the challenging initialization condition of starting from a natural standing pose (neutral stance). Furthermore, in downstream tasks such as obstacle-laden box carrying (Pick-and-Place), it successfully adapted to natural, coordinated whole-body motions purely through language instruction weighting and latent space residual adjustments—without providing any new reference motions.
contributions: Proposed a progressive learning framework using a unified latent space that accumulates diverse skills from different data sources and tasks into a single executable interface.

Decomposed the whole body into arms and body trunk, introducing a deterministic latent space with noise added only in the action space, achieving both improved tracking accuracy and high expressiveness.

Proposed Motion Intuition Distillation (MID) to prevent text-to-motion generation from overfitting to shortcut pathways (like future motion information or initial pose alignment), significantly boosting robustness against unknown initial poses.

Introduced a gating mechanism that dynamically switches between multiple language instructions based on context alongside residual corrections, realizing a lightweight downstream adaptation mechanism that solves complex manipulation tasks without reference motions.

sections.heading: How do you unite scattered skills into a single body?
sections.summary: In physics-based character control, a unified representation to accumulate and reuse diverse skills within a single framework has been lacking. HetSkills solves this challenge by freezing a shared decoder built during tracking control and progressively integrating text generation and task adaptation on top of its latent space.
sections.details:
In physics-based character control, acquiring human-like, natural, composable, and reusable motor skills is the ultimate goal in animation, gaming, and humanoid robotics. Early research focused on imitation learning from small motion capture datasets, which suffered from limited reusability and generality.

Recently, large-scale motion pre-trained models and language-conditioned control have emerged, attempting to elicit motions using words as an interface. However, many existing studies merely use pre-trained models as external guides or regularization terms, failing to form a "shared executable interface" where newly acquired capabilities can be directly incorporated and reused within the same controller.

To tackle this, "HetSkills" was proposed. Here, heterogeneous skills with completely different data sources and supervision formats (motion tracking, text-to-motion generation, motion completion from sparse observations, and downstream task adaptation) are progressively aggregated into a single latent space. To prevent performance degradation from distillation, it uniquely freezes the decoder from the initially learned tracking skill and reuses it directly in subsequent tasks.

sections.heading: The journey from imitation learning to language control and body partitioning
sections.summary: This section surveys prior work across physics-based motion imitation, large-scale motion pre-training including diffusion models, body-part-level control, and task adaptation. Whereas existing methods were constrained by fixed datasets or specific interfaces, HetSkills sets itself apart by developing them in a unified space.
sections.details:
Physics-based motion learning began with reinforcement learning research faithfully tracking reference motion clips. It later evolved into adversarial generation methods to enhance stylistic naturalness, VAE-based approaches to ensure motion diversity, and attempts to utilize diffusion models as behavioral priors. However, these fundamentally assumed a single fixed dataset and uniform supervision, making it difficult to progressively add new data or inputs later on.

Additionally, approaches distilling large-scale data into universal latent spaces and direct learning of thousands of skills from natural language instructions have appeared. Nonetheless, they faced issues such as degradation of original tracking capabilities during distillation steps, or difficulties in reliably retrieving necessary behaviors from an overly vast latent space during downstream tasks.

Regarding body partitioning, its effectiveness has been demonstrated in kinematics-based methods and hierarchical RL, but it has not been used as a unified interface flexibly accommodating heterogeneous input modalities. HetSkills builds a foundation that integrates all heterogeneous skills into the same latent representation while leveraging the benefits of part-based control.

captions.F2: Overall system overview of HetSkills. It shows tracking skill ($\mathscr{F}^{trc}$), motion completion ($\mathscr{F}^{moc}$), text-to-motion generation ($\mathscr{F}^{t2m}$), and downstream tasks ($\mathscr{F}^{task^*}$), each having its own encoder while being executed through a common arm/body latent space and a frozen shared decoder.

sections.heading: How do you formulate a problem with completely different goal signals?
sections.summary: Physics-based character control is formulated as a goal-conditioned Markov Decision Process. Completely different goal signals across skills (future poses, text, keyframes, etc.) are converted into a shared latent variable $z_t$ and mapped to joint torques via a single decoder.
sections.details:
This study formulates physics-based character control as a Goal-conditioned Markov Decision Process (Goal-conditioned MDP). Given state $s_t$ and goal signal $g_t$, the policy selects action $a_t$ and receives reward $r_t$ from the environment. Here, the output action $a_t$ represents target joint angles, which are converted into torques via proportional-derivative (PD) controllers inside the physics simulator.

The core challenge lies in the fact that the modality of goal signal $g_t$ varies entirely depending on the skill. For example, motion tracking uses future target joint positions, text generation uses natural language sentences, motion completion uses sporadic keyframes, and downstream tasks use task-specific observations alongside language instructions.

HetSkills adopts a two-stage architecture where a skill-specific encoder predicts a shared latent variable $z_t$ from goal signal $g_t$, and a shared decoder reconstructs final action $a_t$ from $z_t$ and current state $s_t$. Consequently, when new skills are added later, the framework easily accommodates them by adding an encoder to predict latent variable $z_t$, without retraining the low-level control decoder.

sections.heading: The backbone of HetSkills: progressively building up skills
sections.summary: HetSkills creates a strong foundation by learning a tracking skill, then sequentially stacks text generation, motion completion, and downstream tasks. All skills are unified by standardized task descriptions, allowing seamless execution of long-horizon composite tasks.
sections.details:
The workflow of HetSkills is highly logical. First, it learns tracking skill $\mathscr{F}^{trc}$, constructing a latent space decomposed into arms and body trunk as well as a shared motion decoder. Once training is complete, this decoder is frozen and reused as-is across all subsequent stages. This fundamentally prevents degradation in control performance caused by distillation downstream.

In subsequent stages, skills with different input formats are constructed on top of this frozen foundation. Text-to-motion generation $\mathscr{F}^{t2m}$ produces latent commands from natural language, motion completion $\mathscr{F}^{moc}$ generates latent commands from sparse targets like VR tracking, and downstream tasks $\mathscr{F}^{tsk^*}$ perform residual adjustments aligned with task rewards while leveraging language priors.

Furthermore, all skills are encapsulated by a Standardized Task Description consisting of initialization, execution conditions, and termination criteria. This allows high-level controllers to seamlessly execute skills in sequence as uniform task units, even if their underlying learning algorithms or input modalities differ.

sections.heading: The foundational tracking skill and body-part decomposition
sections.summary: The whole body is decomposed into arms and body trunk to learn a deterministic and compact latent space. After tracking policy training, the state encoder and low-level decoders are completely frozen as shared assets.
sections.details:
- Model Representation (Section 5.1): The character is based on the SMPL model with 69 degrees of freedom. Continuous 6D parameters are adopted for rotation representation. Observations include proprioception $s^t$ (joint angles, velocities, root height, etc.) and future reference poses $g^t$.

- Part-Partitioning Architecture (Section 5.2): The body is split into "arms" and "body trunk." This decouples high-frequency, low-inertia motions like hand gestures and punches from lower-body locomotion and balance control. A shared state encoder $\mathcal{E}_s$ extracts whole-body context features $c^t$, future encoders for arms and trunk predict compact latent commands $z_a^t, z_b^t$, and dedicated decoders $\mathcal{D}_a, \mathcal{D}_b$ convert them into target joint angles.

- Benefits of a Deterministic Latent Space: Using a stochastic latent space (such as a VAE) often causes unstable latent scaling due to exploration noise. HetSkills outputs latent variables deterministically, injecting exploration noise only into the final joint action space. It also introduces latent magnitude regularization $\mathcal{L}_{mr}$ and AR(1) temporal smoothness regularization $\mathcal{L}_{ar}$.

- Training Objective (Section 5.3): Trained via PPO. It maximizes tracking rewards combining global joint positions/rotations, velocities, root height, foot contact rewards, action smoothness, and energy penalties. Once trained, encoder $\mathcal{E}_s$ and decoders $\mathcal{D}_a, \mathcal{D}_b$ are frozen.

captions.F5: t-SNE visualization of the learned latent space. Even without category labels during training, motion types such as locomotion, gestures, and acrobatics form clean clusters, showing that the latent space acquired meaningful structure.

sections.heading: From language to motion: cutting off shortcuts with Motion Intuition Distillation
sections.summary: HetSkills trains a skill that predicts latent variables from text using the frozen decoder. To prevent shortcut issues where policies rely on future frames or perfect initial poses, it introduces Motion Intuition Distillation (MID) to predict motions from random initial states and mismatched histories.
sections.details:
- Shortcut Issue (Section 6.1): When generating motions directly from text, models tend to exploit "easy shortcuts"—predicting future actions based on recent motion histories or slight pose biases rather than truly understanding language semantics. As a result, the motion breaks down when starting from an unseen pose.

- Motion Intuition Distillation (MID Formulation): To resolve this, future pose access is eliminated, forcing the model to infer motions strictly from current observations, language semantics, and incomplete past histories. Specifically, in addition to Reference State Initialization (RSI, probability 0.7) starting from an intermediate reference frame, it introduces Random Memory Initialization (RMI, probability 0.2), where the start state and past history are initialized from the end frame and history of an entirely different clip. This builds robust "motion intuition" capable of transitioning into intended motions from any state based on semantic instructions.

- Architecture and Training (Sections 6.2–6.3): Text embeddings use a pre-trained TMR encoder fed into Transformer-based arm and body encoders. During training, the frozen tracking skill serves as the teacher (expert). Rather than direct comparison in latent space, distillation is performed via L2 loss on the final joint actions $\hat{a}^t$ through the shared decoder, naturally accommodating decoder non-linearities.

sections.heading: Reconstructing whole-body motion from sparse information
sections.summary: This skill reconstructs whole-body motions from spatially sparse signals (like VR tracking) or temporally sparse targets (like keyframe interpolation). It unifies diverse observation conditions as sets of partial goals on the same latent space.
sections.details:
- Unified Formulation (Section 7.1): Sparse observation goals are unified as $\mathcal{O}^t=\{(t_k,\tilde{g}_k^t)\}_{k=1}^K$ (pairs of time offsets and partial goal features). From this information and proprioception, the model predicts latent commands $z_a^t, z_b^t$ and outputs joint actions via the shared decoder.

- VR Tracking (Spatial Sparsity): Only the next-frame states of three end-effectors (head and both hands) are provided. The model must infer physically plausible behavior for unobserved parts like the lower body. It is trained via behavioral cloning (BC) with the first-stage tracking skill as the teacher.

- Motion Interpolation (Temporal Sparsity): Given global target full-body keyframe poses 5–30 frames ahead along with the remaining time, it synthesizes natural motions interpolating sporadic keyframes. This is also trained via behavioral cloning.

- Human-Scene Interaction (HSI): Involves furniture interaction motions (SAMP dataset), such as sitting on chairs or lounging on sofas. Although from a different distribution than tracking data, reinforcement learning enables high-success adaptation without altering the shared decoder.

captions.F7: Scene interaction motions generated by HetSkills (e.g., sitting on chairs and sofas). Using the shared control framework and latent space directly, complex contact motions with various daily furniture items are executed naturally.

sections.heading: Language-guided downstream adaptation: moving without reference data
sections.summary: Pre-trained text-to-motion priors are leveraged to adapt to novel downstream tasks. A gating mechanism (MoE) dynamically blends multiple language instructions alongside a residual module, enabling natural task execution without reference motion data.
sections.details:
- Standardized Task Description (Section 8.1): Every task is defined as a task unit $\mathcal{T} = \langle \text{Init}, \text{Cond}, \text{Term} \rangle$ consisting of Initialization, Condition, and Termination criteria. This cleanly expresses complex, multi-stage long-horizon tasks as chains of units.

- Compositional Task Guidance (Section 8.2): Downstream task goals cannot always be captured by a single phrase. Therefore, multiple candidate instructions (e.g., "walk," "lift box") are provided for arms and trunk, generating multiple latent candidates from frozen text priors. Gating functions $\mathcal{G}_p$ compute weights $\alpha_p^{t,m}$ to blend candidates based on environment states and task observations, adding task-specific outputs from residual modules $\mathcal{R}_p$.

- Adaptation Training (Section 8.3): Pre-trained priors and decoders remain frozen; only lightweight gating functions and residual modules are trained using PPO. To prevent erratic motions when pursuing task rewards, training optimizes objectives with a penalty $\mathcal{L}_{lmp}$ when latent variables exceed $[-0.1, 0.1]$ and a temporal smoothness penalty $\mathcal{L}_{smooth}$.

sections.heading: Behind the scenes: datasets and evaluation tasks setup
sections.summary: Training and evaluation were conducted on the Isaac Lab simulator using heterogeneous datasets including AMASS, HumanML3D, and SAMP. Path following, striking, and a challenging box Pick-and-Place task were designed for downstream evaluation.
sections.details:
- Simulation Setup: Uses ProtoMotions within Isaac Lab, running physics simulation at 120Hz and policy control at 30Hz. Training utilized two NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPUs.

- Datasets (Section 9.1): AMASS was used for tracking and VR/interpolation tasks, filtered for physically valid clips. HumanML3D (2–9 second clips) was used for text generation, and SAMP (containing furniture contacts) was used for scene interactions.

- Downstream Task Design (Section 9.2): Evaluated across three tasks without providing reference motions to imitate:
  - Path Follow: Following randomly generated waypoints across complex terrain.
  - Strike: Approaching randomly placed targets and knocking them down via kicks or pushes.
  - Pick-and-Place: The most challenging task, composed of three stages: Pick-up, Carry-to, and Put-down. The character must squeeze a box with both hands, lift it to a target height, and carry it without dropping.

- Evaluation Metrics (Section 9.3): Tracking is evaluated via MPJPE (Mean Per Joint Position Error) and success rate (maintaining error below 0.5m). Text generation is evaluated via success rates across varied initial poses and TMR retrieval metrics (R-Precision, MedR).

captions.F8: Examples of downstream tasks adapted by HetSkills: (a) Path Follow, (b) Kick-based Strike, (c) Push-based Strike, and (d) box Pick-and-Place. Tasks are naturally executed purely through language instruction blending and residual learning without task-specific reference motions.

sections.heading: Experimental results: overwhelming robustness and smooth task adaptation
sections.summary: In text-to-motion generation, HetSkills achieved an 81.7% success rate from a neutral stance, outperforming existing baselines. In downstream tasks, language-guided priors enabled stable convergence on the challenging lifting task, alongside continuous long-horizon skill execution.
sections.details:
- Tracking and Interpolation (Section 10.1): HetSkills with two-part partitioning achieved high success rates on the AMASS test set even when conditioning on only 1 frame during inference. Increasing partitions from 1 to 5 improved MPJPE from 42.3mm to 35.5mm, but 2 parts provided the best balance of latent interpretability and computational efficiency. It achieved test success rates of 97.8% in VR tracking, 100% in keyframe interpolation, and 96.1% in SAMP furniture interaction.

- Text-to-Motion Generation (Section 10.2): Demonstrated overwhelming performance advantages over MaskedMimic and CLoSD. It achieved a 96.9% success rate (0.5m threshold) when initialized from the ground-truth first frame, and 81.7% when starting from a neutral standing pose. While baselines degraded sharply, ablation studies confirmed that shortcut prevention via MID (especially RMI) was critical.

- Downstream Adaptation (Section 10.3): Prior methods like ASE and PULSE exhibited backward walking during path following or unnatural postures during striking. Furthermore, in the dual-arm Pick-up task, prior methods failed to learn due to constrained exploration spaces, whereas HetSkills converged reliably. Gating weight analysis showed dominant language instructions shifting naturally across task phases, validating the MoE design.

- Long-Horizon Tasks (Section 10.4): Combining standardized task descriptions with an LLM planner, the character completed continuous long-horizon tasks—such as lifting a box onto a desk, walking to a chair to sit down, standing up, and performing acrobatic moves via text—with natural transitions.

captions.F10: Qualitative results across diverse motion completion tasks: (a) human-scene interaction, (b) motion interpolation between keyframes, and (c) VR tracking. Coherent full-body physical motions are accurately recovered from spatially and temporally sparse inputs.

sections.heading: Limitations and future work: rich contacts and real-world deployment
sections.summary: Challenges remain in accumulating larger skill repertoires, covering contact-rich scene interactions, and handling ambiguous language. Future work aims to incorporate contact-aware modules, extend to real humanoid hardware, and explore autonomous LLM failure recovery.
sections.details:
The authors identify two main limitations. First, while validated across representative skill categories, the framework does not fully cover open-ended, complex contact interactions with objects and scenes, nor massive-scale skill accumulation.

Second, text-to-motion generation accuracy degrades on highly complex actions or ambiguous natural language instructions. While MID improves robustness to initial poses, performance remains bounded by dataset text-motion annotation quality, presenting challenges when distinct motions share similar descriptions.

Future work plans to incorporate contact-rich motion data during tracking stages, add contact detection modules, extend control to real-world humanoid robots, and explore high-level LLM planning for automatic skill selection and failure recovery.

sections.heading: Conclusion: a unified latent space paving the future of humanoid control
sections.summary: HetSkills establishes a framework uniting tracking, text generation, interpolation, and downstream adaptation into a single executable latent space. Expanding new skills without altering low-level controllers provides a strong foundation for future large-scale humanoid control.
sections.details:
This paper proposed HetSkills, a framework for progressively learning heterogeneous skills within a unified latent space for physics-based character control. Its key strength is treating the latent space as a shared executable interface, enabling diverse skills from different data sources and supervision signals to coexist and be reused on a single physics decoder.

Through coordinated control via body-part decomposition, shortcut elimination via Motion Intuition Distillation (MID), and dynamic instruction blending for downstream adaptation, it achieves natural and flexible motion synthesis without task-specific reference motions or decoder retraining. This philosophy of progressively accumulating skills into a single body offers profound insights not only for computer graphics animation but also for general-purpose real-world humanoid robotics.

sections.heading: Appendix: implementation details and computational cost
sections.summary: Details on hyperparameters, network architectures, reward formulations, and training times across skills. Staged independent training enables efficient development with modest compute resources.
sections.details:
- Hyperparameters (Appendix A): Uses the Adam optimizer with learning rates of $2\times 10^{-5}$ for policy and prior networks, and $10^{-4}$ for the value function (Critic). Arm and body trunk latent variables are each 64-dimensional (128 dimensions total). Transformer-based modules embed tokens into 256-dimensional features.

- Computational Cost and Training Time (Appendix B): Progressively training stages rather than a monolithic model keeps computational overhead manageable. Using two RTX 5090 GPUs, stage 1 tracking training takes ~2 days, and stage 2 text-to-motion takes ~5 days. Stage 3 interpolation tasks take 1–2 days on a single GPU. Downstream task adaptation completes in under 5 hours on one GPU due to batched language instruction inference.

- Downstream Rewards (Appendix C): Path following incorporates horizontal tracking rewards and energy penalties on 24 leg degrees of freedom. Strike evaluates approach velocity, heading, and target tilt (success at >~78 degrees). Pick-and-Place uses multi-stage dense rewards evaluating grasp force and lifting height (target 0.8m) when both hands are within 0.1m of grasping points.

takeaways: Once a low-level decoder is robustly trained and frozen, subsequent diverse skills (text instructions, completion, task adaptation) can be achieved with high accuracy simply by learning mappings into its latent space.
Keeping latent variables deterministic rather than stochastic (VAE) and adding exploration noise solely in action space stabilizes latent scale while preserving tracking precision.

When learning physical motions from text, introducing random initial poses and mismatched motion histories (RMI) eliminates shortcut dependencies, building robust motion intuition grounded in language semantics.

For downstream adaptation, dynamically blending language priors via a gating mechanism (MoE) with residual corrections enables solving complex contact manipulation tasks (like box carrying) without reference motions.
limitations: Validated skills are currently limited to a few representative categories; accumulation across larger skill repertoires and exhaustive coverage of contact interactions with complex object geometries remain untested.
Vulnerabilities remain regarding ambiguous natural language annotations (such as distinct motions having similar descriptions), posing challenges for nuanced or highly complex actions.
Evaluations are confined to physics simulations (Isaac Lab), without addressing the sim-to-real gap or hardware actuator constraints required for real-world humanoid deployment.
